mainTopic: Sources for הוצאה, הכנסה and four אמות in רשות הרבים; אב versus תולדה; and the מקושש
overview: The גמרא asks where the מלאכה of הוצאה is written, since זריקה is only its תולדה. רבי יוחנן brings משה's command to stop carrying donations into the Levite camp, and a גזירה שוה of העברה with יום הכפורים shows this was on שבת. הכנסה is learned by סברא, but it is only a תולדה. The גמרא then explains what difference the labels אב and תולדה make: they decide how many חטאות a person brings, or, for רבי אליעזר, they are only names. Next the גמרא looks for a source in the משכן for throwing four אמות in רשות הרבים. Every proposal is rejected, and it concludes that all the rules of four אמות are a received tradition. Three opinions then argue over which מלאכה the מקושש did, and a hidden scroll of איסי בן יהודה explains why this matters. Finally, רבי עקיבא says the מקושש was צלפחד, and רבי יהודה בן בתירא rebukes him for revealing what the תורה kept hidden.

steps.title: Where is carrying out written in the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that זריקה is only a subcategory of הוצאה and asks where הוצאה itself comes from in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: After all, throwing is a subcategory of carrying out. So where is carrying out itself written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the Torah source of the main מלאכה of הוצאה, before going further with זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה dealt with זריקה, which is a תולדה that comes from the אב of הוצאה. A subcategory only makes sense once you know the main category. So the גמרא steps back and asks where הוצאה is found in a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: After all / since (introduces an accepted premise)
Throwing an object from one domain to another
A subcategory (a 'child') of a main מלאכה
Carrying out from a private domain to a public domain

phrases.english: Gemara:
After all, throwing is a subcategory of carrying out;
carrying out itself, where is it written?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי זְרִיקָה תּוֹלָדָה דְהוֹצָאָה הִיא, הוֹצָאָה גּוּפַהּ הֵיכָא כְּתִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה about throwing
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the אב מלאכה of הוצאה

steps.title: משה's command to stop bringing donations
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings the פסוק 'ויצו משה ויעבירו קול במחנה'. He explains that משה was in the Levite camp, which was public domain, and told the people not to carry donations out from their private tents.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The פסוק says, 'And משה commanded, and they passed a proclamation through the camp.' Where was משה sitting? In the Levite camp. The Levite camp was public domain. He told Israel: Do not carry out and bring things from your private domain into the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question with a פסוק about the משכן donations. He reads it as משה forbidding carrying from private to public domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people's tents count as רשות היחיד, and the מחנה לויה, where משה sat, counts as רשות הרבים. When משה told them to stop bringing donations, he was telling them to stop carrying from one domain to the other. That act is the מלאכה of הוצאה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
As the verse says:
"And Moses commanded, and they passed a proclamation throughout the camp"
Where was Moses sitting?
In the camp of the Levites,
and the Levite camp was the public domain,
and he was saying to Israel:
Do not carry out and bring
from your private domain to the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הוצאה is learned from משה's command to stop carrying donations from private tents to the public Levite camp

steps.title: Maybe it was a weekday and the work was simply done
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: how do we know this command was on שבת? Maybe משה stopped the donations on a weekday because they already had enough materials.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know he was standing on שבת? Maybe he was standing on a weekday, and he stopped them because the work was complete, as it is written: 'And the work was enough for them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof by pointing out that nothing in the פסוק says it was שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's proof only works if the command was about שבת. The very next פסוק says the materials were already enough, which gives another simple reason to stop donations. If so, the פסוק teaches nothing about הוצאה on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he was standing on Shabbat?
Perhaps he was standing on a weekday,
and it was because the work was completed,
as it is written:
"And the work was sufficient for them, etc."?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's proof
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that משה's command was given on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק itself gives a weekday reason for stopping, that the materials were sufficient, so the proof about שבת may not hold

steps.title: A word link to יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we learn it was a day when work is forbidden through a גזירה שוה. The word העברה appears here and also about יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn 'passing' from 'passing' said about יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן with a גזירה שוה. The steps that follow will spell out how this word link works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word, העברה, appears in both places. That links them, so whatever is true of the day there is also true here. The next step shows the two פסוקים.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this העברה with the מלאכה of carrying. Here it just means a proclamation or שופר sound 'passing' through the land. It is used only as a linking word.

phrases.english: He derives "passing" from "passing"
from Yom Kippur:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: גזירה שוה that shows the day was one on which work is forbidden
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The command might have been given on a weekday because the materials were sufficient
steps.terutzMaskana: The shared word העברה shows the command was given on a day when work is forbidden

steps.title: Laying out the two verses of the word link
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes both פסוקים. 'ויעבירו קול במחנה' appears by the משכן, and 'והעברת שופר תרועה' appears by יום הכפורים. Just as there it is a day when work is forbidden, so too here.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here: 'And they passed a proclamation through the camp.' And it is written there: 'And you shall pass a שופר blast.' Just as there it is on a day that is forbidden, so too here it is on a day that is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the גזירה שוה it just mentioned by quoting both פסוקים side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shofar of יובל is blown on יום הכפורים, a day when work is forbidden. Because of the shared word, משה's proclamation must also have been on a day when work was forbidden, which is שבת. That brings back רבי יוחנן's proof for הוצאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there, so too here

steps.whatToRemember: The source for הוצאה is משה stopping the people from carrying donations from their tents to the Levite camp. The גזירה שוה of העברה with יום הכפורים shows this happened on שבת.

phrases.english: It is written here: "And they passed a proclamation throughout the camp,"
and it is written there: "And you shall pass a blast of a shofar";
just as there, it is on a day that is forbidden,
so too here, it is on a day that is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא וַיַּעֲבִירוּ קוֹל בַּמַּחֲנֶה וּכְתִיב הָתָם וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ שׁוֹפַר תְּרוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the גזירה שוה of step 4
steps.raayaObject: That משה's command was given on a day when work is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא כה:ט, 'והעברת שופר תרועה', said about יום הכפורים

steps.title: What is the source for carrying in?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the source for הוצאה is found, the גמרא asks where we learn that הכנסה is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found carrying out. From where do we know carrying in?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. The פסוק only showed carrying out, so what about carrying in?
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's command was about carrying from private tents into the public camp. Bringing something from public into private is not shown by that פסוק. The גמרא wants a source for that direction as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying in from public to private domain

phrases.english: We have found carrying out;
carrying in, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the finished proof for הוצאה

steps.title: Logic: direction does not matter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with סברא. Both acts move an object from one domain to another, so there is no difference between carrying out and carrying in.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logic. After all, it is from one domain to another. What difference is there to me between carrying out and carrying in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that no פסוק is needed for הכנסה, because simple logic shows it is the same as הוצאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What makes הוצאה forbidden is moving something between two different domains. That same act happens when carrying in. Only the direction is reversed, and direction is not what matters.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is it to me?

phrases.english: It is a logical inference:
after all, it is from one domain to another;

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי אַפּוֹקֵי וּמָה לִי עַיּוֹלֵי!
phrases.english: what difference is it to me whether carrying out or carrying in!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הכנסה is forbidden by logic, since it is also moving an object between domains

steps.title: Carrying out is primary, carrying in is a subcategory
steps.stepSummary: Even though both are forbidden, הוצאה is the אב מלאכה because it is written in the Torah. הכנסה is only a תולדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: However, carrying out is a primary category, and carrying in is a subcategory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes by giving each act its status. הוצאה is the main category and הכנסה is the subcategory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are full Torah prohibitions on שבת. The difference is only in their label. הוצאה comes straight from the פסוק, so it is the אב. הכנסה is learned by logic from it, so it is a תולדה.
steps.confusionAlert: Calling הכנסה a תולדה does not make it a lighter prohibition. On שבת, a תולדה is just as forbidden from the Torah as an אב.
steps.whatToRemember: הוצאה is learned from a פסוק and is an אב מלאכה. הכנסה is learned through סברא and is a תולדה, but it is equally forbidden.

phrases.english: However, carrying out is a primary category,
carrying in is a subcategory.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the logic of step 7 by setting the status of each act
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both הוצאה and הכנסה are forbidden. הוצאה is the written אב and הכנסה is its logically derived תולדה.

steps.title: What is the point of calling one an אב and the other a תולדה?
steps.stepSummary: Both הוצאה and הכנסה make a person חייב, so the גמרא asks why one is called an אב and the other a תולדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, since a person is חייב for this one and also for that one, why is this one called an 'אב' and that one called a 'תולדה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what difference it makes to call הוצאה an אב and הכנסה a תולדה, since you are punished for both anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said הכנסה is only a תולדה. But if the punishment is the same, the label looks pointless. The גמרא wants to know what practical difference the label creates.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since / after all (opens a logical question)
Main category of forbidden work on שבת

phrases.english: Now, since for this one he is liable
phrases.notes: 'This one' refers to הוצאה, carrying out.

phrases.english: and for that one he is liable,
phrases.notes: 'That one' refers to הכנסה, carrying in.

phrases.english: why does he call this one 'a primary category',
and why does he call that one 'a subcategory'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the practical value of the אב/תולדה distinction made in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference there is between an אב and a תולדה if both make a person חייב.

steps.title: The difference: how many חטאות you bring
steps.stepSummary: Two different אבות, or the תולדות of two different אבות, done together make you bring two חטאות. An אב together with its own תולדה makes you bring only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practical difference: if someone does two אבות together, or two תולדות together, he is חייב two חטאות. But if he does an אב together with its own תולדה, he is חייב only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the labels decide how many חטאות a person brings when he does several forbidden works at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אב and its own תולדה count as one family, so they add up to only one חטאת. Two separate families add up to two. That is why the label matters.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical difference that comes out of it
Together, in one lapse of awareness
Sin-offering brought for an accidental sin

steps.confusionAlert: 'Two תולדות' means the תולדות of two DIFFERENT אבות. Two תולדות of the same אב would count as only one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic halachic meaning of the אב/תולדה system for counting חטאות on שבת.

phrases.english: The practical difference is

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי עָבֵיד שְׁתֵּי אָבוֹת בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי,
phrases.english: that if he performs two primary categories together,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי שְׁתֵּי תוֹלָדוֹת בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי —
phrases.english: or alternatively two subcategories together —
phrases.notes: These are subcategories of two different primary categories.

phrases.english: he is liable for two,
but if he performs a primary category and its own subcategory —
he is liable for only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The labels decide how many חטאות are brought. An אב and its own תולדה together give only one.

steps.title: How do the labels matter for רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that a person brings a separate חטאת for a תולדה even when he does it with its own אב. For him, the answer in step 10 does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי אליעזר, who makes a person חייב for a תולדה even when it is done together with its אב, why do they call one an 'אב' and the other a 'תולדה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answer in step 10 does not work for רבי אליעזר. So it asks again what the labels mean according to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, an אב and its own תולדה make you bring two חטאות, just like two separate אבות. So the counting difference from step 10 disappears. The question of step 9 comes back, but only for his opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Together with (in the place of) the אב

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Eliezer,
who holds one liable for a subcategory done together with its primary category —
why do they call this one 'a primary category',
and why do they call that one 'a subcategory'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דִּמְחַיֵּיב אַתּוֹלָדָה בִּמְקוֹם אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 10's answer fails for רבי אליעזר and repeats the question of step 9 for his view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the אב/תולדה labels mean for רבי אליעזר, since for him they do not change the number of חטאות.

steps.title: First answer: an אב was an important work in the משכן
steps.stepSummary: A work that was important in the משכן is called an אב. A work that was not important there is not called an אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A work that was important in the משכן is called an 'אב'. A work that was not important in the משכן is not called an 'אב'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer for רבי אליעזר. For him the labels are only names that show how important each work was in the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר the label does not change the punishment. It reflects history: the works done in an important way in the building of the משכן are the 'fathers'. The other works are named after them.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tabernacle, whose work is the model for the forbidden works

phrases.english: That which was a significant work in the Tabernacle —
he calls it 'a primary category',
that which was not a significant work in the Tabernacle —
he does not call it 'a primary category'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי אליעזר the labels show which works were important in the משכן. They do not change the halacha.

steps.title: Second answer: an אב is written in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: Another option is that a work written in the Torah is called an אב, and a work not written there is called a תולדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: the one that is written is called an 'אב', and the one that is not written is called a 'תולדה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer for רבי אליעזר. The label depends on whether the work is written in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches our סוגיא: הוצאה is written in the Torah ('ויעבירו קול במחנה'), so it is an אב. הכנסה comes only from סברא, so it is a תולדה. That is the same reason given in step 8.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that אב and תולדה are both forbidden. For the חכמים, the labels change how many חטאות you bring. For רבי אליעזר, they are only names: either for importance in the משכן, or for being written in the Torah.

phrases.english: Alternatively: that which is written —
he calls 'a primary category',
and that which is not written he calls 'a subcategory'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 11, next to step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The label depends on whether the work is written in the Torah.

steps.title: The משנה about throwing four אמות against a wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. If an object is thrown four אמות and hits a wall above ten טפחים, it is like throwing into the air. Below ten טפחים, it is like throwing onto the ground, and throwing four אמות onto the ground makes one חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that which we learned in a משנה: one who throws four אמות onto a wall — if above ten טפחים, it is like throwing into the air; if below ten טפחים, it is like throwing onto the ground. And one who throws four אמות onto the ground is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה about throwing four אמות in a רשות הרבים. It is setting up the next question, which will ask where this rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוגיא was just asking where each kind of carrying comes from. Now it brings a new case: moving an object four אמות in a רשות הרבים. The words 'והא דתנן' tell us the גמרא is about to ask for a source for this rule too.

keyTerms.meaning: And that which we learned in a משנה (introduces a source to be discussed)
Four cubits, the distance that makes one חייב in a רשות הרבים
Ten handbreadths, the height limit of a רשות הרבים

steps.confusionAlert: Above ten טפחים the thrower is פטור because the object did not land in the רשות הרבים. It is treated as if it stayed in the air.

phrases.english: And that which we learned in a mishna:
One who throws four cubits onto a wall,
above ten handbreadths —
it is like throwing into the air.
below ten handbreadths —
it is like throwing onto the ground,
and one who throws four cubits onto the ground is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new source question. After finding the sources for הוצאה and הכנסה, the גמרא turns to carrying four אמות in a רשות הרבים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing four אמות in a רשות הרבים makes one חייב if it lands below ten טפחים. Above ten טפחים, it counts as landing in the air.

steps.title: What is the source for throwing four cubits in the public domain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that throwing four אמות inside רשות הרבים makes one חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone threw an object four אמות inside רשות הרבים, how do we know he is חייב?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 14 ended with the rule that throwing four אמות onto the ground makes a person חייב. Now the גמרא asks where that rule comes from. This question opens the whole discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every מלאכה on שבת needs a source in the work done in the משכן. Moving an object from one רשות to another is easy to find there. Moving it four אמות inside the same רשות is harder, because nothing changes domains, so the גמרא needs a separate source.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits, the distance that counts as a real move in רשות הרבים
From where do we know? (a request for a source)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the object does NOT go from one רשות to another. It stays in רשות הרבים the whole time and only travels four אמות. That is why the גמרא needs a different source.

phrases.english: If he threw four cubits in the public domain,
from where do we know that he is liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 14, that throwing four אמות on the ground makes one חייב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source in the משכן for being חייב when moving an object four אמות inside רשות הרבים.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה says the weavers threw needles to each other
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה says the weavers of the יריעות in the משכן threw their needles to each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה said: Because the weavers of the curtains threw their needles to one another.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יאשיה gives a first answer. In the משכן, the workers threw needles to each other, so throwing was a real kind of work there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the workers sat on the ground, which counts as רשות הרבים. When one needed a needle, the other threw it across the space between them. That gives us throwing four אמות inside one רשות as a משכן activity.

keyTerms.meaning: Weavers of the curtains of the משכן

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya said:
Because the weavers of the curtains
throw their needles to one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה: שֶׁכֵּן אוֹרְגֵי יְרִיעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the משכן, workers threw needles to each other, which is throwing four אמות inside one רשות.

steps.title: Weavers do not use needles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why weavers would need needles at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Weavers, what do they need needles for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבי יאשיה's answer. Weaving is done on a loom, not with a needle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is about the details, not the idea. If weavers never used needles, they had no needles to throw, so the answer as stated makes no sense.

phrases.english: Weavers, why do they need needles?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רבי יאשיה's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'weavers throw needles' in step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Weaving does not use needles, so weavers had no needles to throw.

steps.title: Correction: it was the sewers who threw needles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: the people who sewed the curtains threw their needles.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: because the sewers of the curtains threw their needles to one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא corrects רבי יאשיה's statement. Instead of weavers, it was the sewers who threw needles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea stays the same, and only the type of worker changes. Sewers clearly use needles, so the first problem goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a correction or new answer)

phrases.english: Rather, because the sewers of the curtains
throw their needles to one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by correcting the wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual correction (emending the type of worker)

steps.title: Maybe they sat right next to each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe the sewers sat next to each other and just handed the needles over.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they sat next to each other?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof. If the sewers sat close together, they did not need to throw anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if there was real throwing across a distance. If they sat side by side, there was no throw at all.

phrases.english: But perhaps they sat next to each other?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the corrected answer of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the sewers threw needles.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If they sat close together, there was no throw, so there is no source.

steps.title: They would poke each other with needles
steps.stepSummary: They could not sit close, because they would hit each other with their needles.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would reach each other with the needles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the sewers had to sit apart. If they sat close, their needles would poke each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sewing means pulling the needle out with a wide arm motion. Sitting close would cause injuries, so they kept a distance, and that means they had to throw.

phrases.english: They would reach each other with the needles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe they sat side by side.
steps.terutzMaskana: They had to sit apart to avoid hurting each other.

steps.title: Maybe they sat less than four cubits apart
steps.stepSummary: Even if they sat apart, maybe the distance was under four אמות, so the proof fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps they sat within four אמות of each other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבי יאשיה's source. Sitting apart does not prove they sat four אמות apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We need a throw of at least four אמות. Sitting far enough apart to avoid needles may still be less than that. So the needle case cannot be the source, and the גמרא will look for a new one.

phrases.english: Perhaps they sat within four cubits?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Even after accepting step 20, it shows the proof is still not enough.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יאשיה's whole source from the needle-throwers.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no proof that the distance between them was a full four אמות.

steps.title: רב חסדא: weavers threw the shuttle across the cloth
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the source is weavers throwing the shuttle through the cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: Because the weavers of the curtains throw the shuttle through the cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first source failed, רב חסדא offers a new one. While weaving, the weaver throws the shuttle across the curtain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Weaving means sending the thread across the cloth by throwing the shuttle. Weaving clearly happened in the משכן, and the throw goes across the width of the cloth.

keyTerms.meaning: The weaver's shuttle, a tool that carries the thread
A curtain, the cloth being woven

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said:
Because the weavers of the curtains
throw the shuttle into the curtain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: שֶׁכֵּן אוֹרְגֵי יְרִיעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected source of רבי יאשיה with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Throwing the shuttle while weaving is the משכן source.

steps.title: But the weaver holds the thread in his hand
steps.stepSummary: This is not a real throw, because the weaver keeps hold of the thread.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't he hold it tied in his hand?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. The weaver still holds the end of the thread, so the shuttle never fully leaves his hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being חייב for throwing requires the object to leave the thrower completely. If part of it stays connected to his hand, it is not a full throw.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so? (introduces a challenge)
He holds it tied in his hand

phrases.english: But doesn't he hold it tied in his hand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's answer in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that throwing the shuttle is a real throw.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The thread stays in the weaver's hand, so the object never fully leaves him.

steps.title: It means the final throw
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא means the last throw, when the weaver lets go of the thread.
steps.simpleTranslation: With the last thread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב חסדא means the very last throw, at the end of the weaving. Then the weaver lets go completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the thread stays in his hand. At the final pass he releases it, so the shuttle fully leaves him and it counts as a real throw.

keyTerms.meaning: The final thread, the last throw

phrases.english: With the final thread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every throw of the shuttle, while the thread is still held.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the final throw, when the thread is let go.

steps.title: But the shuttle moves through an exempt area
steps.stepSummary: The shuttle travels over the narrow cloth, which is a מקום פטור, not רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it travels in a מקום פטור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. The shuttle moves over the cloth on the loom, and that cloth is too narrow to be a real רשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We need a throw of four אמות inside רשות הרבים. The cloth is less than four טפחים wide, so it is a מקום פטור, and throwing there does not make one חייב. So the weaving throw cannot be the source.

keyTerms.meaning: An exempt area, a place that is neither a public nor a private domain

phrases.english: But it travels in an exempt place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Even after the fix in step 24, it raises a new problem with the throw across the cloth.
steps.kashyaTarget: The shuttle-across-the-cloth version of רב חסדא's source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The throw happens in a מקום פטור, not רשות הרבים, so it cannot teach a rule about רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Weavers threw the shuttle to those who borrowed it
steps.stepSummary: The new version: weavers threw the shuttle on the ground area to other weavers who asked to borrow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: because the weavers of the curtains throw the shuttle to those who ask to borrow it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes רב חסדא's source. The throw was not across the cloth. It was from one weaver to another who asked to borrow the shuttle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the shuttle flies through the open ground between the workers, which is רשות הרבים, not over the cloth. This removes the מקום פטור problem.

phrases.english: Rather, because the weavers of the curtains
throw the shuttle to those who borrow it from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שֶׁכֵּן אוֹרְגֵי יְרִיעוֹת זוֹרְקִין בּוּכְיָאר לְשׁוֹאֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 by changing which throw is the source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The throw across the cloth is the source.
steps.terutzMaskana: The throw to a borrowing weaver, through רשות הרבים, is the source.

steps.title: Maybe the weavers sat right next to each other
steps.stepSummary: Same challenge as before: maybe the weavers sat close and did not need to throw.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they sat next to each other?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same challenge it used on the sewers. If the weavers sat close, they could just hand the shuttle over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof needs real distance between the workers. Without it, there is no throw.

phrases.english: But perhaps they sat next to each other?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 26 the same way step 19 challenged step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the weavers threw the shuttle to borrowers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If they sat close, there was no real throw.

steps.title: They would bump each other at the edge of the cloth
steps.stepSummary: Weavers had to sit far apart, or they would bump each other while pulling the thread at the edge of the cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would reach each other at the edge of the cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that weavers needed lots of room. When they pulled the thread at the edge of the cloth, they would bump into each other if they sat close.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Weaving a large curtain needs a wide space for the arm movements at the edges. So the weavers sat far apart, and throwing the shuttle to a borrower would be a real throw. This defense does not hold for long: steps 29-31 attack it (staggered seating, no borrowing, and no source for carrying), and step 32 concludes that the rules of four אמות are a received tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: The edge or hem of the cloth, where the thread is pulled tight

phrases.english: They would reach each other at the edge of the cloth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27. Steps 29-31 then challenge this answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the weavers sat side by side.
steps.terutzMaskana: Weavers sat far apart, so throwing the shuttle to them was a real throw in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Maybe the weavers sat staggered
steps.stepSummary: The weavers could have sat in a zigzag pattern. Then they could sit close without bumping, and they would not need to throw.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they sat staggered (in a zigzag)?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer, which said the weavers had to sit far apart so they would not bump each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer said that sitting close in a straight line would cause bumping. But if the weavers sat in a zigzag, they could be close without bumping. Then they could hand the shuttle over directly, and we lose the proof that they threw it.

phrases.english: But perhaps they were staggered?!
phrases.notes: A zigzag seating lets people sit close without hitting each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 28 (the weavers had to sit far apart).
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the weavers had to sit far apart.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different seating pattern removes the need for distance, so there was no need to throw.

steps.title: The weavers never borrowed from each other
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of לודא learns from a פסוק that each craftsman worked only with his own materials. So nobody asked to borrow a shuttle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, did they borrow from one another? Didn't לודא teach: 'each man from his work which they were doing'? This means each one worked from his own work, and not from his friend's work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second attack. It goes after the core of step 26, which said that weavers threw the shuttle to others who asked to borrow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'איש איש ממלאכתו' are read to mean that each worker had his own tools and supplies. If nobody borrowed, nobody threw a shuttle to anyone. So the whole case of throwing in the משכן falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא whose ברייתא is quoted

phrases.english: And furthermore, did they borrow from one another?
But didn't Luda teach:
"Each man from his work which they were doing" —
he works from his own work,
and he does not work from his friend's work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent attack on the borrowing case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that weavers borrowed shuttles from each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that each worker used only his own tools, so no borrowing took place.

steps.title: Carrying 4 אמות still has no source
steps.stepSummary: Even if throwing could be learned from the משכן, there is still no source for carrying (מעביר) 4 אמות in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: one who carries 4 אמות in רשות הרבים — from where do we know that he is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third, broader attack. Even if the throwing case works, carrying by hand is still unexplained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weaver case only shows throwing. It does not show walking while holding something for 4 אמות. So this approach leaves a whole part of the halacha without a source.

keyTerms.meaning: one who carries/moves an object along

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ: מַעֲבִיר אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
phrases.english: And furthermore: one who carries four cubits in the public domain —
from where do we know that he is liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: מַעֲבִיר אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מְנָלַן דְּמִחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third objection that widens the problem from throwing to carrying.
steps.kashyaTarget: The whole attempt to find a משכן source for 4 אמות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even a successful throwing proof would not cover carrying, so the method is incomplete.

steps.title: All 4 אמות rules are a received tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives up on finding a source in the משכן. All the rules of 4 אמות in רשות הרבים come from tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: all the rules of 4 אמות in רשות הרבים were learned as a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the whole back-and-forth. The rules of 4 אמות are not learned from the משכן at all; they are a tradition handed down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attempts to learn throwing from the weavers ran into one problem after another. So the גמרא concludes that the rules of 4 אמות, both throwing and carrying, are a received tradition. The pattern in the משכן is not their source.

keyTerms.meaning: they learned it as a received tradition

steps.whatToRemember: The איסור of moving something 4 אמות in רשות הרבים, by throwing or carrying, is a received tradition. It is not learned from the work in the משכן.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'גמרא' does not mean the Talmud. It means a teaching received by tradition.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: כׇּל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
phrases.english: Rather: all of four cubits in the public domain —
they learned it by tradition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כׇּל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים גְּמָרָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the objections by dropping the search for a source in the משכן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rules of 4 אמות in רשות הרבים are a received tradition.

steps.title: שמואל: the wood-gatherer carried 4 אמות
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the מקושש (the man killed for gathering wood on שבת in the מדבר) did the מלאכה of carrying 4 אמות in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the מקושש was one who carried 4 אמות in רשות הרבים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: which מלאכה did the מקושש do? שמואל gives the first opinion, which connects to the topic of 4 אמות just discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the מקושש was stoned for breaking שבת but does not name the exact מלאכה. שמואל says it was carrying 4 אמות. That also shows the 4 אמות rule was already in force in the days of משה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The wood-gatherer — one who carries four cubits
in the public domain, he was.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מְקוֹשֵׁשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the source of 4 אמות to a related case: the מקושש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מקושש was liable for carrying 4 אמות in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: ברייתא: he detached branches
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the מקושש did the מלאכה of detaching (תולש), pulling growing wood from the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: he was one who detached (plants from the ground).
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second opinion about the מקושש's מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the sin was cutting or pulling growing branches, which is a form of קוצר. It was not about moving them.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
He was one who detached.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different opinion from שמואל's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מקושש was liable for detaching.

steps.title: רב אחא: he gathered sticks into a pile
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רבי יעקב says the מקושש did the מלאכה of מעמר, gathering things into a bundle or pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רבי יעקב said: he was one who gathered sticks into a pile.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third opinion about the מקושש's מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the sin is collecting the sticks together, which is the מלאכה of מעמר. It was not carrying them and not pulling them from the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: one who gathers produce into a pile or bundle

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa son of Rabbi Ya'akov said:
He was one who gathered.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: מְעַמֵּר הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion, alongside the first two.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מקושש was liable for gathering (מעמר).

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference it makes which מלאכה the מקושש did.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why it matters which of the three opinions is right. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The event already happened, and he was stoned either way. So the גמרא wants a reason that matters for halacha today.

keyTerms.meaning: what practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the three-way disagreement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The halachic difference between the three opinions about the מקושש.

steps.title: רב's hidden scroll: one חטאת for all 39 מלאכות
steps.stepSummary: The difference relates to רב's statement. רב found a hidden scroll in רבי חייא's house quoting איסי בן יהודה: there are 39 אבות מלאכות, and if someone did all of them in one העלם, he brings only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters for what רב said. רב said: I found a hidden scroll in the house of רבי חייא, and written in it was: איסי בן יהודה says, the אבות מלאכות are 40 minus 1. If someone did all of them in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the question by bringing in a statement from רב. The full link to the מקושש will become clear in the coming lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איסי בן יהודה's ruling seems to say that doing many מלאכות in one העלם brings only one חטאת. This statement will turn out to matter for deciding which מלאכות are definitely חייב. That is where the מקושש comes in.

keyTerms.meaning: a hidden scroll (private notes of teachings)
the main categories of forbidden work

phrases.english: For that of Rav, as Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: מָצָאתִי מְגִלַּת סְתָרִים בֵּי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
phrases.english: I found a hidden scroll in the house of Rabbi Ḥiyya,

phrases.aramaic: וְכָתוּב בָּהּ, אִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: and written in it: Isi ben Yehuda says:
The primary labors are forty less one,
and if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness,
he is liable for only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכִדְרַב, דְּאָמַר רַב: מָצָאתִי מְגִלַּת סְתָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the practical-difference question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference connects to איסי בן יהודה's teaching in רב's hidden scroll about the count of 39 מלאכות and how many חטאות one brings.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן says one is liable for each מלאכה
steps.stepSummary: Only one? A משנה counts 39 מלאכות, and רבי יוחנן explained that the count is there to teach that one is liable for each מלאכה separately, even in one העלם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only one and no more? But we learned in a משנה: the אבות מלאכות are 40 minus 1. And we asked about it: why do I need the number? And רבי יוחנן said: so that if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges איסי בן יהודה's 'only one חטאת' from a well-known explanation of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the number 39, and רבי יוחנן says the number is there to count separate חטאות. So doing all 39 in one העלם brings 39 חטאות, not one. That directly contradicts the wording in the scroll.

keyTerms.meaning: and we discussed it / raised a question on it
why do I need the number?
liable for each and every one

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next answer, which will fix the wording of איסי בן יהודה's statement. That fix is what finally shows why the מקושש's מלאכה matters.

phrases.english: One and no more?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: אֲבוֹת מְלָאכוֹת אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אַחַת,
phrases.english: But we learned: The primary labors are forty less one,
and we discussed it: Why do I need the number?
And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
That if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness —
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the statement quoted in step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: איסי בן יהודה's claim that one is liable for only one חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's number 39, as רבי יוחנן explains it, teaches a separate חטאת for each מלאכה done in one העלם.

steps.title: Correcting the hidden scroll's wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the scroll's text to read: 'he is not liable for one of them.' This means one of the 39 מלאכות does not carry the death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: he is not liable for one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the last step by changing the words of איסי בן יהודה's scroll. It does not mean 'one חטאת for all of them.' It means 'there is one מלאכה that you are not liable for.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old reading clashed with רבי יוחנן, who says you bring a separate חטאת for each מלאכה. The new reading says something different: one of the 39 אבות מלאכות does not carry מיתה. The scroll does not say which one, and that sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead. Used to correct or reread a text.
He is not liable (here: not liable for the death penalty).
One of them, meaning one of the 39 מלאכות.

steps.confusionAlert: The new reading does NOT mean that this mystery מלאכה is allowed on שבת. It is still a forbidden אב מלאכה. It is only an exception when it comes to the death penalty.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַל אַחַת מֵהֶם.
phrases.english: Say instead: he is not liable for one of them.
phrases.notes: There is one מלאכה that does not carry the death penalty, and the scroll does not name it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from רבי יוחנן's reading of the 39 count.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation (changing the wording of the source)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The scroll means that all 39 מלאכות in one העלם need only one חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The scroll means that one unnamed מלאכה out of the 39 does not carry the death penalty.

steps.title: Each opinion is sure its own מלאכה carries the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, the ברייתא, and רב אחא בר יעקב each hold that the מלאכה they assign to the מקושש is certainly punishable by death. So that מלאכה cannot be the unnamed one in the scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious to רב יהודה that carrying is liable. It is obvious to the ברייתא that detaching is liable. It is obvious to רב אחא בר יעקב that gathering is liable. Each one holds: at least this מלאכה is not in doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now answers the question from step 36: why does it matter which מלאכה the מקושש did? The answer is that the מקושש was stoned, so his מלאכה is surely a death-penalty מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scroll leaves us unsure which מלאכה is free of מיתה. Each opinion removes one מלאכה from that doubt: the one they say the מקושש did. רב יהודה says carrying (העברה) is certain, the ברייתא says detaching (תולש), and רב אחא says gathering (מעמר).

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries four אמות in the public domain.

steps.whatToRemember: The argument over the מקושש's מלאכה matters in practice. Whatever he did is certainly a death-penalty מלאכה, so it cannot be the one the scroll excludes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the loop that began with the question 'מאי נפקא מינה' (what practical difference does it make). It shows that even a story from the תורה can decide a halachic doubt.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דְּהַמַּעֲבִיר חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: It is obvious to Rav Yehuda that one who carries is liable,
phrases.notes: He holds that the מקושש carried four אמות.

phrases.english: and it is obvious to the baraita that one who detaches is liable,
phrases.notes: Here 'מתניתין' means the ברייתא from step 34.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דִּמְעַמֵּר חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: and it is obvious to Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov that one who gathers is liable.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר הָא מִיהַת לָא מְסַפְּקָא,
phrases.english: This Master holds: this one, at least, is not in doubt,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר הָא מִיהַת לָא מְסַפְּקָא.
phrases.english: and that Master holds: that one, at least, is not in doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דְּהַמַּעֲבִיר חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the corrected scroll to explain the practical difference asked about in step 36.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each opinion is certain that the מקושש's מלאכה carries the death penalty, so it is not the unnamed exception in the scroll.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא teaches that the מקושש was צלפחד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי עקיבא's teaching that the מקושש was צלפחד. He learns it from the shared phrase 'in the desert' in two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: the wood gatherer was צלפחד. The פסוק says, 'The children of Israel were in the desert, and they found a man.' Later the תורה says, 'Our father died in the desert.' Just as there it means צלפחד, so too here it means צלפחד. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about the מקושש: who was he? רבי עקיבא names him as צלפחד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'במדבר' (in the desert) shows up in the story of the מקושש. It also shows up when the daughters of צלפחד say their father 'died in the desert, in his own sin.' רבי עקיבא links the two with a גזירה שוה and concludes that the unnamed man is צלפחד.

keyTerms.meaning: The wood gatherer who broke שבת in the desert.
The father of the five daughters who asked for a share of the land.
Below, meaning in a later passage.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The wood gatherer is Zelophehad,
and so it says:
"And the children of Israel were in the desert,
and they found a man, etc.",
and later it says:
"Our father died in the desert,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:3, the words of צלפחד's daughters.

phrases.english: just as there it is Zelophehad,
so too here it is Zelophehad —
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about who the מקושש was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through a גזירה שוה on 'במדבר', רבי עקיבא teaches that the מקושש was צלפחד.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירא objects: either way you will be held accountable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא warns רבי עקיבא that he is wrong in both possible cases. If he is right, he revealed what the תורה chose to hide. If he is wrong, he is slandering a צדיק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא said to him: עקיבא, either way you will have to answer for this. If you are right, the תורה hid him and you are revealing him! And if not, you are spreading a bad name about that צדיק.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן בתירא attacks רבי עקיבא's teaching. He does not attack the proof itself. He attacks whether it was proper to say it at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument has two sides, and both lead to trouble. If the identification is true, the תורה left the man unnamed on purpose to protect his honor, so revealing him is wrong. If it is false, then calling an innocent man a שבת-breaker is slander.

keyTerms.meaning: To give an accounting, to be judged (in Heaven).
Covered him, kept his identity hidden.

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a lasting lesson: when the תורה leaves a sinner's name out, there is value in not exposing him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira said to him:
Akiva, either way
you will in the future have to give an accounting:
if it is as you say —
the Torah concealed him,
and you reveal him?!
and if not —

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה מוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק.
phrases.english: you are spreading slander about that righteous man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's identification from step 41.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's teaching that the מקושש was צלפחד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided problem: if the teaching is true, it exposes what the תורה deliberately hid. If it is false, it slanders a צדיק. Either way, saying it is wrong.
